human_name: NBPF gene family / Olduvai (DUF1220) cluster on chromosome 1

GRCh38.note: NBPF family is dispersed across chr1: 1p36 (NBPF1 ~16.56 Mb), 1p13/1p11 satellite block, and the 1q21.1-q21.2 expansion (~145-149 Mb) where the bulk of high-copy NBPF8/NBPF9/NBPF10/NBPF11/NBPF14/NBPF15/NBPF19/NBPF20 paralogs reside; coordinates here are bounding-box not contiguous segdup

copy_count_typical: 250-350 Olduvai domain copies per diploid human; ~24-30 NBPF paralog genes in GRCh38
architecture_note: NBPF is the canonical 'core duplicon' family (Jiang 2007). The unit of duplication is the ~1.6 kb Olduvai triplet (HLS1-HLS2-HLS3 = three exons encoding two Olduvai domains), embedded in larger HOR (higher-order-repeat) blocks of variable size that have expanded primarily in 1q21.1-q21.2 plus a satellite block at 1p11.2 / 1p36.13. The locus does NOT have a single tandem-dup unit; it is a mosaic of nested expansions. structural_architecture='intrachromosomal_interspersed' is the dominant geometry but several paralog pairs cross into 'interchromosomal' (1p<->1q).

diagnostic_features.psv_strategy_note: PSV-level discrimination between individual NBPF paralogs is not feasible from a small SNP table because (a) inter-paralog identity exceeds 99% over the Olduvai HOR, (b) paralogs are not in stable 1:1 correspondence across haplotypes — copy number varies 250-350 Olduvai domains per diploid, (c) HPRC R2 + T2T-CHM13 are the first assemblies to fully resolve the cluster. For LLmap T1, the discriminator is the *HOR pattern* (Olduvai triplet composition + flanking unique-anchor sequence), not point variants. Downstream tools should treat NBPF reads as multi-position mappings by default.

olduvai_triplet_structure.unit: HLS1 + HLS2 + HLS3 exons encoding two Olduvai domains (~65 aa each)
olduvai_triplet_structure.note: Sikela 2018 / Dougherty 2018 nomenclature paper (F1000Res, after originally published 2017). HLS = Human-Lineage-Specific exons.

copy_number_evolution.note: Largest human-lineage-specific coding copy-number expansion in the genome.

satellite_block_1p11.note: 1p11.2 satellite (NBPF8 locus) is a known interchromosomal jump from the 1q21.1 cluster; one of the few NBPF paralogs reliably anchored outside 1q.

primary.note: k=25 / mm=4 chosen because intra-cluster identity routinely exceeds 99% and a single Olduvai HOR copy can carry 1-3 point differences in a 25 bp window. With mm=2 a large fraction of reads would chain-fail. Mapping must NOT require unique chains — multi-mapping is expected and correct.

fallback_chain.name: relaxed_mismatch
fallback_chain.rationale: deep Olduvai HOR convergence may need wider tolerance

fallback_chain.name: chain_only
fallback_chain.rationale: extension across HOR seams generates spurious indels

fallback_chain.name: multi_position
fallback_chain.rationale: NBPF reads SHOULD multi-map — single-best-hit is wrong here

fallback_chain.name: llm_checkpoint
fallback_chain.trigger: novel HOR pattern not in catalog
fallback_chain.rationale: evaluate triplet composition against known NBPF1-30 patterns

fallback_chain.name: novel_haplotype_flag
fallback_chain.rationale: report total Olduvai-domain count rather than gene-level assignment when paralog cannot be determined

test_cases.note: T2T-CHM13 v2.0 provides the first complete sequence-level resolution of 1q21.1 NBPF cluster (Vollger 2022); use as reference truth set
HPRC R2 + diploid assembly available; NBPF copy-number quantifiable

primary_sources.note: Sikela JM, van Roy F, Sigrist CJA, Bateman A, Bruford EA — joint nomenclature paper renaming DUF1220 -> Olduvai (Dougherty/Sikela group co-authored). F1000Research. This is the canonical Olduvai-domain reference.

Jiang Z, Tang H, Ventura M et al. — Ancestral reconstruction of segmental duplications reveals punctuated cores of human genome evolution. Nat Genet 39:1361-1368. Defines NBPF as the prototype 'core duplicon'.
Vollger MR et al. — Segmental duplications and their variation in a complete human genome (T2T-CHM13). Science 376:eabj6965. First sequence-complete view of the NBPF 1q21.1 cluster.

supporting_databases: UCSC genomicSuperDups (hg38) — captures the 1q21.1 NBPF block as a dense SD cluster
T2T-CHM13 v2.0 SD-BED (Vollger 2022) — primary truth set
HPRC R2 pangenome (Liao 2023 + 2026 update) — haplotype copy-number variation
HGNC NBPF gene family page — paralog naming NBPF1..NBPF30
provenance.db_coverage_note: NBPF is well represented in UCSC SD-BED but individual paralog boundaries shift between GRCh38 and T2T-CHM13 because GRCh38 collapses several Olduvai HOR copies. Use CHM13 + HPRC R2 as primary; GRCh38 coordinates here are approximate region bounds.
